title: Conjecture 2
statement_text: For every $n$-vertex graph $G$, the extension complexity of $\mathrm{COR}(G)$ is $2^{\Omega(\mathrm{tw}(G)+\log n)}$.
context_text: Graphs are simple. The correlation polytope $\mathrm{COR}(G)$ of $G=(V,E)$ is the convex hull in $\mathbb{R}^{V\cup E}$ of the vectors $(\chi(X),\chi(E(X)))$ for $X\subseteq V$, where $E(X)$ is the set of edges with both ends in $X$ and $\chi$ denotes characteristic vectors (in machine learning it is the marginal polytope). A polytope $Q$ is an extension of $P$ if $P$ is an affine image of $Q$, and the extension complexity of $P$ is the minimum number of facets of an extension of $P$. The authors prove the upper bound $2^{O(\mathrm{tw}(G)+\log n)}$ for every $n$-vertex graph (via Kolman and Koutecký), that extension complexity of $\mathrm{COR}$ is minor-monotone, and that the conjectured lower bound holds for every graph in a proper minor-closed class; for every graph their proof gives $2^{\Omega(h+\log n)}$ with $h$ the largest height of a grid minor, hence $2^{\Omega(\mathrm{tw}(G)^{\delta}+\log n)}$ for some universal $\delta>1/20$ by the polynomial grid-minor theorem. If true, the conjecture would improve the bound $2^{\Omega(n/\log n)}$ of Göös, Jain and Watson for stable set polytopes (convex hulls of stable sets) to $2^{\Omega(n)}$, and would yield explicit $0/1$-polytopes with extension complexity exponential in their dimension, as predicted by a counting argument of Rothvoß.
notes: The paper proves this conjecture for the special case of proper minor-closed graph classes (Theorem 3), but the general statement remains open.
paper_title: Extension Complexity of the Correlation Polytope
